The '''Fréchet derivative''' is a [[derivative]] that finds a [[linear map|linear operator]] that approximates a [[function]] $f:\mathbb{C}^m \to \mathbb{C}^n$ near a given point.

== Formal definition ==

Let $X,Y$ be [[vector space]]s over $\mathbb{C}$, $f:X \to Y$ be a [[function]].

If

$$
\exists L\in \mathcal{B}(X,Y) \text{(bounded linear operator)}, \\
f(\vec{x}_0+\vec{h})=f(\vec{x}_0)+L(\vec{h})+o(\|\vec{h}\|)
\qquad (\vec{h}\to 0),
$$
where $\vec x_0, \vec h \in X$, $o(\|\vec{h}\|)$ is a [[o(x) and o(x)|small-o]] function of $\|\vec h\|$,

then $L$ is the '''Fréchet derivative''' of $f$ at $\vec x_0$.

Equivalently,

$$
\lim_{\|\vec{h}\|_X\to 0}
\frac{\|f(\vec{x}_0+\vec{h})-f(\vec{x}_0)-L(\vec{h})\|_Y}{\|\vec{h}\|_X}=0.
$$
